# Process the warranty returns

Customers ask for warranty replacements through tickets in the `tickets` service. Products and stock are kept in the `inventory` service. You can use both through the `tickets` and `inventory` MCP servers.

Every open ticket labeled `warranty` is a claim. The warranty policy is the open ticket labeled `warranty-policy`: it decides which claims are covered, what to ship and from which warehouse. A replacement is shipped with one `adjust_stock` call: the replacement sku, the warehouse, delta minus the claim's units, reason `shipment`, reference `RMA-<ticket id>`.

Colleagues shipped some replacements before you without answering the tickets. A claim whose reference already has a `shipment` adjustment has been shipped: ship nothing more, and answer it with that adjustment.

Two open claims for the same serial are one claim. The one with the higher ticket id is a duplicate of the other: answer it as a duplicate and do nothing else for it. This rule comes before every other.

Process the claims one at a time in ticket id order, lowest id first, so that each one sees the stock the ones before it left. Add exactly one comment to each claim and set its status:

- Shipped, by you or before you: `Replacement <sku> shipped from <warehouse> as <adjustment id>.` with the sku and warehouse of the shipment and its adjustment id (for example `adj-123`). Status `resolved`.
- Not covered: `Not covered: <reason>.` with the reason the policy gives. Status `closed`.
- Covered, but no warehouse can ship it: `Backordered: <sku>.` Status `pending`.
- Duplicate: `Duplicate of #<ticket id of the other claim>.` Status `duplicate`.

Ship nothing for a claim that is not covered, backordered or a duplicate. Leave every other ticket and all other stock as they are. Each `adjust_stock` call records a new adjustment, even when repeated with the same arguments.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
I'll start by discovering the tools on the two MCP servers.

{"server":"tickets","tool":"mcp_tickets_get_ticket","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":1102,\"title\":\"Warranty returns policy\",\"body\":\"Warranty returns policy, revision 2026-08, in force since 2026-08-01.\\n\\nScope: open tickets labeled `warranty`. Each one is a claim for the product (sku), serial, purchase date, units and region in its body.\\n\\nCoverage by product line, which is the item's `category` in inventory, counted from the purchase date:\\n- power-tools: 24 months\\n- outdoor: 24 months\\n- kitchen: 12 months\\n- batteries: 12 months\\n- accessories: not covered\\n\\nA claim is within its warranty when the ticket was created (UTC date) on or before the same calendar day N months after the purchase date. For example, a 24 month warranty on a product bought 2024-03-05 covers claims created up to and including 2026-03-05.\\n\\nRefurbished units have serial numbers that start with `RF-`. Their warranty is 6 months, whatever the product line; accessories stay not covered.\\n\\nEach serial is replaced at most once. When an earlier warranty ticket already got a replacement for the same serial (a `shipment` adjustment under its reference `RMA-<ticket id>`), a new claim for that serial is not covered.\\n\\nCheck a claim in this order and stop at the first rule it fails: product line (reason `product line excluded`), serial (reason `serial already replaced`), warranty period (reason `warranty expired`).\\n\\nReplacement: the same sku, as many units as the claim names. When the sku is discontinued, its item name gives the successor as `(replaced by <sku>)`; ship the successor instead.\\n\\nWarehouse: ship from the warehouse that serves the customer's region:\\n- atlantic: east\\n- pacific: west\\n- central: north\\n\\nWhen that warehouse holds fewer units of the replacement than the claim needs, ship from the other warehouse that holds the most units of it, if that is enough (on a tie, the first in alphabetical order). Never split a replacement across warehouses. When no warehouse holds enough, the claim is backordered.\\n\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":\"P4\",\"team\":\"returns\",\"customer\":\"returns-ops@example.com\",\"labels\":[\"warranty-policy\"],\"created_at\":\"2026-09-01T08:00:00Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-09-01T08:00:00Z\",\"comments\":[]}"}]}}

steps.message:
I processed all 25 open warranty claims in ticket id order. Each claim has one comment and its status set. I ran no final check of every ticket and adjustment, only 1106's comment (one comment, correct) and the `adj-107` shipment. `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

- **Shipped (15, resolved):**
  - **By me (14):** 1107, 1108, 1113, 1114, 1117, 1120, 1122, 1123, 1124, 1126, 1127, 1133, 1134 and 1135.
  - **Before me (1):** 1125 was answered with the existing `adj-102`, and I shipped nothing more.
  - **Successor sku:** 1127 shipped `PT-1219`, because `PT-1203` is discontinued.
  - **Fallback warehouses:** 1133 shipped from north because west had run out after 1107. 1122 shipped from north, which held exactly 1 unit.
- **Not covered (8, closed):**
  - **Warranty expired:** 1106, 1110, 1115, 1116 and 1118.
  - **Product line excluded:** 1121 and 1128.
  - **Serial already replaced:** 1132, because 1103 already got `adj-24` for the same serial.
- **Backordered (1, pending):** 1130 needs 2 units of `PT-1209`. East and west each hold only 1, so nothing shipped.
- **Duplicate (1, duplicate):** 1131 has the same serial as 1108 and was answered as "Duplicate of #1108."

Two calls failed with errors along the way. The `adjust_stock` call for 1107 timed out, but a check showed it had been recorded as `adj-107`, so I did not repeat it. The comment on 1106 hit a connection reset, and the retry with the same idempotency key left a single comment.

I left the already-resolved or closed warranty tickets (1103, 1105), the pending 1112 and the policy tickets alone.
